nodes.summary: The Harris inequality (Harris 1960): under the product Bernoulli(`p`) measure on a finite configuration space, increasing events are positively correlated, `P_p(A) * P_p(B) ≤ P_p(A ∩ B)`. No measurability hypothesis is needed since `E` is finite. See also `IsUpperSet.le_card_inter_finset` (Harris–Kleitman, counting form).
nodes.title: Harris inequality

nodes.summary: Events depending only on `S` are closed under arbitrary unions.
nodes.title: Events depending on a coordinate set are closed under unions

nodes.summary: Events depending only on `S` are closed under intersection.
nodes.title: Events depending on a coordinate set are closed under intersection

nodes.summary: An event depending only on the coordinates in `F` is the cylinder over its section on `F`.
nodes.title: Finitely dependent event is a cylinder over its section

nodes.summary: If the indicator of `A` depends only on the coordinates in `S` (Mathlib's `DependsOn`), so does the event `A` (`StatMech.DependsOn`).
nodes.title: An event depends on the coordinates its indicator depends on
Monotonicity of the closed filling map

nodes.summary: The configuration on `E` equal to `η` on the finite set `F` and closed (`false`) off `F`.
nodes.title: Filling a finite configuration with closed coordinates

nodes.summary: Positive correlation passes to limits of decreasing sequences of measurable events: if `μ(A n) μ(B n) ≤ μ(A n ∩ B n)` for all `n`, the same holds for `⋂ n, A n` and `⋂ n, B n`.
nodes.title: Positive correlation passes to decreasing intersections

nodes.summary: The Harris inequality on a countable configuration space for increasing events that depend on finitely many coordinates: `P_p(A) * P_p(B) ≤ P_p(A ∩ B)`.
nodes.title: Harris inequality for finitely dependent increasing events

nodes.summary: If the event `A` depends only on `S`, so does its indicator function.
nodes.title: Indicator of an event depends on the coordinates the event depends on

nodes.summary: The section of an increasing event is increasing.
nodes.title: Section of an increasing event is increasing

nodes.summary: The section of an event `A` on `F`: the configurations `η` on `F` with `ih_fill F η ∈ A`.
nodes.title: Section of an event on a finite coordinate set

nodes.summary: Continuity from above of a finite measure, real-valued form: `μ.real (A n)` tends to `μ.real (⋂ n, A n)` for a decreasing sequence of measurable sets.
nodes.title: Continuity from above of a finite measure, real-valued form

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
